decisions.reason: F4 incorrectly strengthened the cutoff conclusion from vanishing outside U to support contained in U, and step 4.1 used that unsupported conclusion. For symmetric open V with V+V contained in U, every x in closure(V) belongs to V-V=V+V, so the supplied cutoff vanishes off V and its support lies in closure(V) contained in U. The normalized symmetric product is therefore admissible. Also supplied the real/imaginary approximation argument needed for complex Lp. Statement unchanged; the sigma-finite support reductions and all-pair net remain valid.

The supplied definition defaults Cc(G) to real functions. On Z real convolution squares are even, so their complex span cannot approximate delta_1 in L1 or L2; f plus/minus i h in polarization is also inadmissible. Replaced every generator and polarization input by explicit Cc(G;C), extended real density componentwise, proved convolution continuity using L1 translation continuity, and checked the polarization expansion and positive Gram integral. The intended complex density claim is preserved; the Statement now explicitly changes its scalar interface.

F3 and step 5.1 selected one kernel for every neighbourhood, which DC does not supply. Replaced this family throughout by the directed net of all admissible pairs i=(U,u). Multiplicativity with a fixed f0 having h(f0) nonzero then gives h(u_i) tending to 1 and the Bochner convolution identity gives h(f)=integral f conjugate(gamma). The translation ratio, bounded unitization character, uniqueness test integral, and Bochner prerequisites were checked. A direct support estimate now proves each Fourier evaluation nonzero with norm one without assuming its nonzeroness first. Statement unchanged.

The real Cc density supplier cannot directly approximate complex f: on the one-point mass-one group f=i has distance at least one from every real function. F3 now explicitly approximates the real and imaginary parts and recombines them, and F2/steps 1.1 and 2.1 use Cc(G;C). The Fourier bound gives uniform convergence of the continuous transforms. Compactness of the unitization character space gives compact superlevel sets disjoint from q, yielding full uniform vanishing at infinity. AC/DC and the theorem statement are unchanged.

The bare F6 Minkowski citation omits its sigma-finiteness hypothesis; the translation supplier does supply the needed restricted-product bounds, so that omission alone is nonfatal. Independently, original step 1.4 fatally invokes real Cc density for complex f and normalisation on a complex convolution not licensed by its real-generator interface. F6 now states the support restrictions explicitly. The replacement step 2.1 inverts only real positive q_i, promotes that a.e. identity to everywhere by continuity and Haar positivity, and uses Fubini on sigma-compact essential supports of f and phat(q_i), with absolute integral ||f||1 ||phat(q_i)||1. Compact dual tails and a global L1 subsequence then prove f=fvee a.e.; Statement unchanged.
